name: SGLang
notable_features: RadixAttention: a radix tree over the KV cache so any shared prefix, not just an exact-prefix match, is reused
SGLang language primitives (radix cache, jump-forward decoding, LPM cache-aware admission) are exposed as first-class knobs
Strong RL-rollout story: the same engine is used to generate training rollouts, and SGLang Diffusion adds image/video generation in the same package
OpenAI-compatible server, a Rust component in the tree, and sgl-router for multi-model routing
Separate backends for TPU (SGL-JAX and SGL-torchtpu) alongside the main PyTorch path
Speculative decoding across six method families - EAGLE-2/EAGLE-3, MTP, UNO, DFLASH, standalone small draft models and NGRAM - with the docs naming EAGLE-3 as the recommended speed/quality choice

The strongest measured speculative-decoding result in this repo, and the only one that is a controlled within-engine A/B: DSPARK on 8x RTX PRO 6000 takes prose decode from 36.4-36.5 tok/s to 76.5-78.9 tok/s and structured decode from 36.5 to 120.3-120.5 tok/s at block_size=2, with acceptance 3.0 vs 1.0 tokens/step
hardware_caveats: CUDA 13 is required: the CUDA 12.9 wheel/image lane is retired because PyTorch 2.14 publishes no CUDA 12.9 builds, and SGLang 0.5.19 is the last release with a CUDA 12 lane

FlashInfer is the default attention backend and only supports sm75 and above; on sm75+ devices with FlashInfer problems the documented fallback is --attention-backend triton --sampling-backend pytorch
Many dependencies publish pre-release wheels only, so uv installs silently land on an old version (0.5.9) unless --prerelease=allow is passed

The documented supported-hardware list is narrower than vLLM's: NVIDIA A100/H100/H200/H800/H20/B200/B300/GB200/GB300 plus select RTX 30/40/50, and AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI350X/MI355X. No consumer AMD Radeon entry
TPU support is split across sibling projects (SGL-JAX, SGL-torchtpu), so TPU parity with the main CUDA path is not automatic
Apple Silicon and Intel support exist but are documented on separate hardware-platform pages with far less detail than the NVIDIA path

SGLang's MoE rank computation divides by zero if ep_size exceeds tp_size (moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)), so a plausible-looking parallel configuration can fail at launch rather than degrade

--enable-expert-parallel is a vLLM flag and is REJECTED OUTRIGHT by SGLang, which takes ep_size instead; and a container that does not receive TP_SIZE/DP_SIZE/EP_SIZE explicitly silently serves TP8 defaults, so a 'new' configuration can never have happened while the logs look healthy - verify via /get_server_info before timing anything

On 8x RTX PRO 6000 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash the run is COMMUNICATION-BOUND, not compute-bound: ~87% GPU utilization at 220 W of a 600 W cap, with ~7K tok/s prefill described as the ceiling for a board without NVLink. This is the number to check before blaming the scheduler
best_for: Agentic and RL workloads where many requests share long, branching context - the radix cache reuses partial prefixes, not just exact ones
Serving latency-sensitive multi-turn conversation, because prefix reuse removes the re-prefill of chat history
Teams that want to experiment with scheduling policy rather than just tune it
avoid_for: Environments pinned to CUDA 12 - there is no supported lane any more
Installs where a silently downgraded dependency is acceptable risk; the pre-release dependency set is a real operational hazard
Consumer AMD Radeon cards, which are not in the documented support list
notes: Scheduling terms: 'radix-cache' is the distinguishing mechanism (radix tree over KV blocks); 'prefix-cache' is used here in the looser sense that the radix cache provides prefix reuse generally. AMD entry is Instinct-class only per the README's supported-hardware table. TPU and NPU paths are separate projects, so 'tpu' here means supported but not first-class in this repo. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0 months), latest release v0.5.21 published 2026-10-02 - a release two days before this record's date, which is a strong liveness signal - 1996 contributors, open_issues_count 5553 (issues PLUS pull requests), NOT archived, 36777 stars. DEPLOYMENT: the STRONGEST production evidence in the entire engine dataset, graded YES with numbers attached - see [[ev-production-evidence-is-scarce-and-nearly-always-single-site]]. SGLang issue #40877 (2026-09-23, open) self-describes as 'Field data from running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash as a production SGLang backend on 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only - no NVLink)' with the operator stating the numbers 'come from a working day of production use'. Published benchmarks with full conditions are in [[ev-sglang-dsv41-production-128k-prefill-tps]], [[ev-sglang-dsv41-production-decode-tok-s-per-user]], [[ev-sglang-dspark-spec-decoding-2x-decode-ab]] and [[ev-sglang-dsv41-prefix-cache-hit-prefill-speedup]]. The method quality is worth noting because it is the standard this repo holds numbers to: configuration verified server-side via /get_server_info rather than assumed, timing taken from the response `usage` field rather than SSE chunk counts, and a repeat leg (6,765 vs 6,853 tok/s, -1.3%) establishing run-to-run variance. The operator also documents the trap that corrupted their own earlier measurements - trusting container env vars produced 'a full sweep of false data' before they added a config gate. SELF-DECLARED LIMITS, which are why the numbers are citable as production evidence: 'No 24 h soak', block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised. Configuration traps documented on this model: DP2 x TP4, prefill context-parallel and --enable-dp-attention alone are all rejected or silently no-op, with the error 'V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A'. BUILD COST: no published figure found for SGLang's source compile. Its issue #6830 ('On deepseek, it often takes tens of minutes') refers to torch.compile and CUDA-graph CAPTURE at server startup, which is a JIT/startup cost rather than a source build, and it is too thin to record as a number - see [[ev-build-cost-is-three-separate-builds]]. FEATURE AXES: chunked prefill and prefix caching were already recorded; disaggregated routing exists via the model gateway ('Add EPD (Encode-Prefill-Decode) Disaggregated Routing Support'); structured output is UNSTATED and was not confirmed from the pages read.
